stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Opponents of municipal taxes on sugar-sweetened beverages have often described such levies as ______: because lower-income households devote a greater portion of their budgets to these drinks, the tax claims a larger share of their income than it does of wealthier households' income. A 2021 analysis of one city's tax complicated this charge, however. Those same households cut their purchases most sharply once the tax took effect, and so stood to gain the most from the resulting drop in diabetes risk.
explanation: The colon tells you the blank is defined by what follows it. The opponents' complaint is that the tax takes a larger share of income from poorer households than from wealthier ones. That is exactly what "regressive" means: a tax whose burden falls proportionally harder on people with less income. The 2021 finding pushes back on the charge by pointing to who benefits. It doesn't redefine the charge, so the blank still has to name the income-share complaint.

A.why: You chose a criticism that people really do make of soda taxes: that the government is overriding personal choices. You matched the topic, not this sentence. The colon spells out the complaint, and it is about how much of each household's income the tax takes. It says nothing about restricting freedom of choice.

C.why: You noticed that the burden falls on poorer households and picked a word with roughly the right negative tone. But "punitive" means meant to punish. The opponents in the passage describe how the cost is distributed. They never claim the tax was designed to punish anyone, so this word claims more than the text supports.

D.why: You may have read ahead to the reduced purchases and taken "prohibitive" to describe them. A prohibitive cost is high enough to stop people from buying at all. The opponents' complaint only makes sense if households keep buying and keep paying the tax, since that is how it 'claims a larger share' of their income. The word clashes with the definition after the colon.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Clay can hold a surprising quantity of water: in some deposits, the open space between particles exceeds 40 percent of the sediment's total volume, far more than in many sandstones. Yet clay layers make notoriously poor aquifers. Because those spaces are minute and only weakly connected to one another, clay is nearly ______, transmitting water so slowly that a well drilled into it may yield almost nothing for years.
explanation: The "because" clause gives you the logic. The spaces in clay are tiny and poorly connected, so water barely moves through it, and a well yields almost nothing. The blank has to mean 'does not let water pass through.' That is "impermeable." The passage separates two properties. Clay has plenty of space for water (it is highly porous) but almost no ability to move it (it is nearly impermeable). The answer must name the second property without denying the first.

A.why: This is the trap that survives the key insight. You correctly worked out that clay blocks the flow of water, then reached for the familiar word that seems to say so. But "nonporous" means having no open spaces, and the first sentence says clay's open space can be more than 40 percent of its volume. Clay is porous. What it lacks is permeability.

B.why: You picked a word that sounds like it is about water and solids. "Insoluble" means 'does not dissolve.' Whether clay dissolves has nothing to do with how slowly water moves through it, and that is the property the sentence describes.

D.why: You may have connected 'yields almost nothing' to dryness. "Desiccated" means thoroughly dried out, but the passage stresses that clay holds a large quantity of water. The well fails because the water can't flow out, not because there is none.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Excavators at a Bronze Age hillfort long assumed that its ramparts had been raised in a single campaign. Cross-sections of the walls, however, show dozens of thin layers of packed earth separated by turf lines, each representing roughly one season's work, spread across about two centuries. This ______ building process suggests that the fort was less a planned stronghold than a structure its community kept adding to.
explanation: "This ___ building process" refers back to the description of many thin layers, each added in a different season over two centuries. The final clause confirms it: the community "kept adding to" the fort. "Accretive" means growing by gradual addition, so it fits exactly, even though it is the least familiar word on the list.

A.why: "Concerted" means planned and carried out jointly, all at once. That describes the single campaign the excavators assumed, which is the view the evidence overturns. You put the rejected view into the blank.

B.why: You may have chosen "fragmentary" because the walls are made of separate layers. But "fragmentary" means broken or incomplete, and nothing says the ramparts are unfinished. The layers add up to a whole wall. This is a word that looks like the idea you wanted but means something else.

D.why: "Provisional" means temporary, put in place until something permanent arrives. The passage says the work was gradual, not that each phase was meant to be replaced.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: The belief that static stretching before a sprint protects against muscle strains was once so pervasive that many coaches treated it as ______: a principle too obvious to need testing. When controlled trials were finally run, they found no reduction in strain rates, and several recorded a small loss of sprint speed.
explanation: The blank describes how coaches treated the belief, and the colon defines it: "a principle too obvious to need testing." "Axiomatic" means taken as self-evidently true without proof. The later trials disprove the belief, but they don't change how coaches regarded it back then.

B.why: "Apocryphal" means of doubtful truth, and the trials do show the belief was unfounded. But the blank describes how coaches saw it, and they saw it as obviously true. You correctly spotted the reversal and then put the trials' verdict on the coaches' side of it.

C.why: "Contentious" means disputed. A belief so widespread that few thought to test it was the opposite of disputed.

D.why: "Empirical" means based on observation or testing. The passage says the belief went untested until the trials, so it was not empirical.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Three evenly spaced dips in the brightness of a distant star could signal a planet passing in front of it on each orbit. Dark starspots rotating across the star's face, however, can produce the same pattern, and the observations so far cannot tell the two apart. The team therefore described the dips as ______ evidence of a planet, pending further monitoring.
explanation: "Therefore" ties the blank to the previous sentence: the data fit two explanations equally well and "cannot tell the two apart." "Equivocal" means open to more than one interpretation, which is exactly that situation. "Pending further monitoring" shows the team still considers a planet possible.

A.why: "Conclusive" means settling the question. The data cannot tell a planet from starspots, so nothing is settled.

B.why: "Spurious" means false. You saw that the dips aren't proof and pushed further, to calling them wrong. The team hasn't ruled a planet out. That is why they plan further monitoring.

D.why: "Anomalous" sounds like an astronomy word, but it means unusual or departing from the norm. The point is that the evidence is ambiguous, not that it is strange. You matched the topic instead of the logic.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Since the industry began, platform companies have described their delivery couriers as independent contractors free to choose when and where they work, and the contracts still use that language. Yet because the platform alone sets pay per order, assigns orders by algorithm, and can deactivate any account without explanation, couriers' independence remains largely ______.
explanation: The contracts call couriers independent, but the platform controls pay, assignments, and access. So the independence exists mostly in name. "Nominal" means existing in name only, which matches that contrast between the contract's wording and the working reality.

A.why: You correctly saw that little real independence exists. But "vestigial" means a leftover trace of something that used to be fuller, and the passage says the arrangement has been this way "since the industry began." Nothing has shrunk, so the word adds a history the text rules out.

B.why: "Inalienable" means impossible to take away. The platform can deactivate any account without explanation, so the independence can be taken away at any time.

C.why: "Tacit" means implied but never stated. The independence is stated outright in the contracts, so this is a word that sounds like "hidden" but means the wrong thing.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When the woodcuts were first exhibited, critics dismissed their jagged, uneven lines as ______, the marks of a printmaker who had not mastered the knife. The surviving blocks tell a different story: on each one, the same artist cut hair-fine lines elsewhere, reserving the rough strokes for figures in motion.
explanation: The blank is part of the critics' view, and the phrase after it defines that view: the lines looked like the work of someone who "had not mastered the knife." "Maladroit" means clumsy or lacking skill. The blocks later disprove the critics, but the blank reports what they thought.

A.why: "Studied" means deliberate and carefully planned. That is what the blocks reveal, not what the critics claimed. You read the reversal correctly and then put its conclusion on the wrong side.

C.why: "Meretricious" is negative, like the critics, but it means showy and superficially attractive. The critics complained about lack of skill, not cheap glamour, so the tone matches and the meaning doesn't.

D.why: "Derivative" means copied from others' work. The critics' complaint was about technical control of the knife, not originality.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: After a congested highway was widened from four lanes to six, rush-hour travel times fell for about two years and then returned to their former levels: the added capacity had drawn drivers who previously avoided the route. Many planners now regard such widenings as ______ at best, since they ease congestion for a time without addressing the demand that causes it.
explanation: The widening relieved the symptom (travel times) temporarily without touching the cause (demand). "Palliative" means relieving symptoms without curing the underlying problem, which is exactly the distinction the "since" clause draws.

B.why: "Remedial" is the familiar word that roughly means "fixing." But a remedial measure corrects a problem, and the passage says the widening left the cause untouched and the problem returned. It fits roughly but not exactly.

C.why: "Prophylactic" sounds medical, like the right answer, but it means preventive. The widening responded to congestion that already existed. It prevented nothing.

D.why: "Salutary" means beneficial in a lasting, wholesome way. The passage says the benefit faded after two years, and "at best" signals a limited judgment, not praise.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: After wolves returned to the valley, streamside willows that had been browsed nearly to the ground began to recover. The study's authors note, however, that the same decade brought unusually wet summers, which also favor willow growth. Their conclusion is accordingly ______: wolves were probably one cause of the recovery, though not necessarily the main one.
explanation: "Accordingly" links the conclusion to the authors' caution about a second possible cause. The colon then shows the conclusion: a real claim ("probably one cause") with careful limits. "Circumspect" means cautious and attentive to the full circumstances, which describes a conclusion that commits to something while hedging it carefully.

A.why: "Categorical" means absolute and unqualified. The conclusion is hedged twice, with "probably" and "not necessarily the main one."

B.why: You saw the hedging and took it too far. "Agnostic" would mean the authors declined to take any position on the cause, but they do take one: wolves were probably a contributor. Careful is not the same as uncommitted.

C.why: "Tendentious" means slanted to promote a particular view. Raising a rival explanation against their own finding is the opposite of slanted.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Cut off from imported indigo during the war, dyers in the region turned to woad, a locally grown plant that yields a paler and less colorfast blue. Buyers knew exactly what they were getting, and they paid less for it. Because the cloth was bought only when indigo could not be had, merchants' ledgers from the period treat woad-dyed cloth as ______ goods.
explanation: "Because" ties the blank to the fact that woad cloth was bought only when the real thing wasn't available. It was also visibly inferior and priced lower. "Ersatz" means an inferior substitute for something better, and it fits every one of those conditions.

A.why: You correctly saw that woad stood in for indigo. But "counterfeit" means an imitation meant to deceive, and the passage says buyers "knew exactly what they were getting." A substitute is not a fake when no one is fooled.

B.why: "Vernacular" means local or native, and woad was grown locally. But the "because" clause is about being a substitute, not about being local. You matched an incidental detail.

D.why: "Anachronistic" means out of its proper time. It sounds right for a history passage, but nothing here is about timing. You matched the topic, not the logic.
